clue.text: Hard week hosting a supporter of war

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone has a tough seven days while putting up a warmonger as a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a hawk is someone who favours aggressive military action, the opposite of a dove.

clue.text: Increase number of animals at home?

definitions.meaning: to raise a level or rate
taken as more pets: read upwards as a down light runs, the first word spells them

explanation.surface: A household wonders about acquiring more creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: STEP written going up, as a down light runs, reads PETS, animals kept at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or raise the level of something, such as output, is a common phrasal-verb synonym for boosting it.

clue.text: Expressions of courage and audacity in a jam

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is British slang for cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone shows bravery and cheek while stuck in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE (nerve) and NECK (cheek) are both informal British words, which is why they can pair as 'expressions of' courage and audacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam forms at a narrowing in the road, the classic congestion point.

clue.text: Italian gangster: "I run Italian city, turning up in criminal acts"

indicators.note: the reversed group sits inside the other letters
criminal suggests the letters of acts are twisted out of order
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
Roma is the Italian name of Rome

explanation.surface: A mobster boasts in quotation that he controls an Italian city by showing up during crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses I, R and ROMA to give AMORRI, which goes 'in' CSTA, an anagram of ACTS signalled by 'criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camorra is the Neapolitan crime syndicate, and a member of it is so named.

clue.text: Grouse, or another main course?

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to grumble, and a complaint is slang called this
grouse is a game bird served as a main, and this meat is another such dish

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether to order the game bird or some other dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface treats grouse as food, which is half the trick: the first sense is the complaint, and the second plays on grouse being eaten too.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a complaint or grievance; it is also the meat of cattle served as an entrée.

clue.text: English Literature picked up in item of coverage

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters means reading them from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A school subject is collected as part of what a newspaper reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' does not signal a homophone here: in a down entry it reverses E LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof or floor slabs are pieces that cover a surface, one unit of coverage.

clue.text: A lot of Republicans will accept it (public relations) as a political tool

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the party letters take the others inside

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Many Republicans will embrace spin as a weapon in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP (Grand Old Party) is the usual nickname of the US Republican Party; the inserted pair lands after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, especially in art or literature, used as an instrument of persuasion.

clue.text: See Fenland city invaded by the men rioting ferociously

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the city is entered by the jumbled men, who end up inside it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in the Fens of Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: rioting men are in disorder, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Look at a city in eastern England being stormed by a violent mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying former marshland in eastern England; Ely is its cathedral city. V (vide) is the Latin 'see' used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe acting with intense force and passion, a near synonym.

clue.text: Sort of heavenly model: one with lots bare, wiggling

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: wiggling things squirm around, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A model posing for an artist, naked, with plenty of wriggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly model' tempts towards a beautiful person, but it means a model of the heavens. 'wiggling' rearranges LOTS BARE into STROLABE.
explanation.definitionFit: This old instrument maps the positions of stars, a working representation of the sky.

clue.text: Unmarried, having no son? A cosy position

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away

parts.note: an unmarried person is single
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A childless bachelor is asked whether his life is comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireside or hearth, a warm snug spot by the fire.

clue.text: Broke? Increase in receipts mostly reversed

indicators.note: reversed means the remaining letters are read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
the word for increase is placed inside the receipts

parts.note: takings or receipts are the take
UP means increase, as in prices going up

explanation.surface: A trader asks if going bankrupt follows a fall in earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increase in receipts' reads as one phrase about rising income, but 'in' is the insertion signal; 'mostly' drops the last letter before 'reversed' turns the rest round.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken or finished is the sense; this German-derived word means bust or out of order.

clue.text: Misaligned fellows having little money in aggregate

indicators.note: the fellows and the coin go inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is mineral rock, a natural aggregate of minerals
F is fellow, so FF is fellows
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Lopsided men with hardly any cash between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in aggregate' looks like 'in total', but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'aggregate' is the mineral rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not placed at the middle point is out of alignment.

clue.text: Subprogram to do with energy? It bears fruit

parts.note: an applet is a small program run within another application
RE means about or concerning
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A query about whether a piece of code concerns power, with a productive result.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard plant producing pomes is the plain sense; the fruit is the crop it carries.

clue.text: It captures brief life-story in caper relating to medical treatment

indicators.note: the combined letters are placed inside the prank word

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper or prank

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so the first word takes the short life story in

parts.note: taken as written
bio is short for biography

explanation.surface: A short biography is put into a comic escapade with a medical theme.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIOT, from 'It captures' BIO, goes 'in' ANTIC as ANT...IC.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes drugs that fight bacterial infection, so it relates to medical care.

clue.text: Exalting Knight: none right to be upset about that

indicators.note: upset suggests being knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is raised in honour, though nobody thinks it proper and is annoyed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' rearranges N with NONE RIGHT; 'about that' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing on a throne means raising to the highest honour, so it carries the sense of elevating.

clue.text: Run in footwear? I need special shoes

indicators.note: the run letter goes inside the hosiery word

parts.note: hose are stockings or socks, worn on the feet
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone asks about jogging in socks, and replies that they need proper trainers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer itself: a creature that must be shod with iron shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Farriers nail iron shoes to this animal's hooves, so it is the one that needs special footwear.

clue.text: Standard approach employs limits of theory when in difficulty

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the trouble word

parts.note: being in a hole means being in trouble
to employ something is to use it

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A conventional method makes use of the boundaries of theory when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in difficulty' reads as a time phrase, but 'in' is the insertion signal and the difficulty is being in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's rules for spelling and layout are its usual way of doing things, its norm.

clue.text: Tense ramble, having shaken off daughter and ferocious mother

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: shaking off something gets rid of it, so that letter goes

parts.note: to digress is to ramble away from the subject
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A nervous wander after getting away from a daughter, with a fierce mum in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the big striped cat is a byword for fierce protective motherhood.

clue.text: One officer I left throttled by chap fully acknowledging blame

indicators.note: being throttled means held in someone's grip, so these letters sit inside the man

parts.note: a chap is a guy, the whole word used
I is the Roman numeral one
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A soldier says he left after being strangled by a man who fully admitted fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fully' tells you to use the whole word for chap, not a shortened form; the four inserted pieces land before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a way that shows one knows one is at fault is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Proclaim appearance of politician in real-time

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the word for real

parts.note: real means true
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A news item about a famous politician showing up live.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous politician's surname is a decoy sitting in plain view; the politician of the wordplay is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something loudly and publicly, as with a fanfare, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Reliable performer dropped in error?

definitions.meaning: a dependable, helpful person is called this in informal British usage
to drop one, in British idiom, is to make a tactless blunder

explanation.surface: A dependable actor is let go by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping a brick' is British slang for making a social gaffe, so the thing dropped stands for the error.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone this praises them as solid and dependable, like a building block.

clue.text: Rough bale carried by a pale 15 without demur

indicators.note: being carried by something means sitting within it

parts.note: 15 across is horse, and a pale horse is a grey

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters are roughly handled and jumbled

explanation.surface: A light-coloured horse bears a rough bundle of hay without complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points to the answer at 15 across, horse; a grey is a pale horse. 'Rough' scrambles the bale before 'carried by' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something willingly and pleasantly means acting with no objection.

clue.text: Resist before the French collapse

parts.note: to buck a trend is to resist it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Holding out before the French give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way under pressure, as a beam bends and fails, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: A great number in lively dance company being held back

indicators.note: held back means turned round, so the company letters within the dance are reversed

parts.note: a cotillion is a brisk French dance for several couples

explanation.surface: A large crowd turns up at a dance troupe's energetic show.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance already contains CO at its start; 'being held back' reverses just those two letters, swapping them to OC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the number one followed by 27 or 48 zeros, an enormous figure.

clue.text: Hero's award — not another award?

indicators.note: not means without, so the smaller honour is removed from the larger one

parts.note: a medallion is a large medal awarded as an honour
a medal is another honour

explanation.surface: A query whether a brave person's honour is anything but a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'Hero', with ''s' as a link: take MEDAL from MEDALLION.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave, celebrated person is often described as a big cat, the king of beasts.

clue.text: Long to marry after losing first husband

indicators.note: losing the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to wed after their first spouse is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or crave something is to have an urge for it.

clue.text: Despicable character keeping Bill silent

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: tit is British slang for a contemptible fool
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A rotter holds on to an invoice and keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood without being stated, so unspoken, is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Betting system supplying sum before end of race

parts.note: to tot up is to add up, so a tot is a sum

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A wagering scheme gives you an amount before the race finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is a pool betting system where winners share the stakes, known by this short form.

clue.text: I attempt to secure line over construction of ice

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so the attempt takes the line inside

parts.note: a go is an attempt
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fasten a rope over an ice building.
explanation.definitionFit: This dome-shaped Inuit shelter is built from blocks of packed snow and ice.

clue.text: Tin left in food store not ultimately suited to a romantic dinner?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the shop word

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word before it is taken

explanation.surface: A tin left at a delicatessen turns out to be wrong for a romantic meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ultimately' looks like a denial but gives T, the final letter of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by flickering wax lights is the atmosphere of an intimate meal for two.
